questions.prompt: What question best captures the craftsman mindset in this chapter?
choices: A) What is this job giving me emotionally today?
B) What valuable thing am I getting better at building here?
C) How quickly can I know whether this is my one true calling?

explanation.gentle: The craftsman mindset turns attention toward skill, value, and output. It does not begin with asking for emotional confirmation.
explanation.direct: This chapter defines the craftsman mindset through outward construction rather than inward fit-monitoring.
explanation.competitive: The new scoreboard is about value built, not reassurance received.

questions.prompt: Why does Jordan Tice matter as an anchor for this chapter?
choices: A) He shows patient craft organized around the work itself rather than around self-display
B) He proves that modest people never care about recognition
C) He shows that every career should start in music

explanation.gentle: Tice gives the chapter a concrete example of attention disciplined by craft rather than by image.
explanation.direct: The example matters because it embodies the chapter's alternative: output-centered ambition instead of identity performance.
explanation.competitive: He matters because the work is at the center, not the self-story.

questions.prompt: What changes when someone shifts from the passion mindset to the craftsman mindset?
choices: A) Work becomes painless
B) Difficulty disappears once the right field is found
C) Rough patches are more likely to be interpreted through skill and value rather than immediate mismatch

explanation.gentle: The chapter does not promise easy work. It promises a steadier way to read difficulty by asking what it is building or revealing.
explanation.direct: The craftsman lens changes interpretation, not the existence of friction. Difficulty becomes easier to sort and use.
explanation.competitive: Pain stays. Automatic verdicts lose authority.

questions.prompt: Maya is in a hard sprint and starts asking whether the project proves the role is wrong for her. Which chapter-based move is strongest?
choices: A) Ignore the project entirely and wait for a more inspiring one
B) Ask what valuable capability the sprint is helping her build before deciding what the discomfort means
C) Assume the project is good because all hard work is meaningful

explanation.gentle: The craftsman mindset redirects the evaluation. Maya should first ask what skill, output, or leverage the sprint is building.
explanation.direct: This matches the chapter's core move from fit anxiety to contribution analysis.
explanation.competitive: Make the sprint pay rent in skill before you let it vote on your future.

questions.prompt: Which statement best preserves the chapter's limit around bad environments?
choices: A) The craftsman mindset means staying in any job if you can work hard enough
B) Contribution focus is useful only when the environment still offers a path for craft, skill, or value to deepen
C) If you leave a bad setting, you were never using the craftsman mindset correctly

explanation.gentle: The chapter keeps a real boundary. Outward focus is strategic, not blind, and it fails in dead or exploitative environments.
explanation.direct: That answer captures the growth-path condition the chapter insists on preserving.
explanation.competitive: No compounding, no mandate. Bad systems can still fail the test.

questions.prompt: A professor hears Elise interpret repetitive practice as proof that music may not be for her. What chapter-based response is strongest?
choices: A) Reframe the repetition around the specific control or technical gain it is building
B) Tell Elise that repetition never matters in serious craft
C) Tell Elise that all doubts are signs she should switch fields

explanation.gentle: The chapter asks Elise to interpret repetition through craft rather than through identity panic.
explanation.direct: A craftsman lens names the technical gain instead of letting repetition become evidence of mismatch by default.
explanation.competitive: Make the drill identify its leverage before it gets treated like betrayal.

questions.prompt: Carter keeps asking whether drawing is his true thing and feels worse after every imperfect page. What shift best fits the chapter?
choices: A) Turn the session into a craft review focused on one technical standard rather than on identity proof
B) Stop drawing until the identity question feels settled
C) Judge every page by whether it confirms long-term destiny

explanation.gentle: The chapter suggests lowering self-absorption by making the standard more technical and concrete.
explanation.direct: Carter should replace existential evaluation with craft evaluation. That is the attentional shift the chapter argues for.
explanation.competitive: Stop asking the sketchbook to certify the self. Raise the standard on the page instead.

questions.prompt: Jonah reviews an old role and realizes he spent most of the year asking whether it matched his identity. According to the chapter, what should he examine now?
choices: A) Whether the role made him feel inspired every morning
B) Whether the role helped him improve output, standards, or portable capability even if it felt imperfect
C) Whether everyone else admired the role more than he did

explanation.gentle: The craftsman lens asks what the role was helping him build, not whether it delivered constant emotional confirmation.
explanation.direct: This is the right postmortem question because it reveals whether the role was generating future leverage through skill and output.
explanation.competitive: Audit what stacked, not what flattered.

questions.prompt: Why does the craftsman mindset often make work feel clearer even when the work is still hard?
choices: A) Because it removes all ambiguity from careers
B) Because it gives difficulty a steadier interpretation through standards, skill, and value creation
C) Because it guarantees external recognition will arrive quickly

explanation.gentle: The chapter says clarity comes from a better lens, not from easier work. Difficulty becomes easier to read when contribution is the focus.
explanation.direct: The craftsman mindset lowers interpretive noise by sorting friction through craft and value rather than through unstable identity questions.
explanation.competitive: A stronger scoreboard makes the same pain easier to diagnose.

questions.prompt: What pressure does this chapter create for the next one?
choices: A) To explain what resource accumulates when better output keeps compounding
B) To prove that emotional fit never matters again
C) To rank different kinds of modesty

explanation.gentle: Once the craftsman mindset shifts attention to value and output, the next question is what that improvement becomes over time.
explanation.direct: The chapter points directly toward the resource generated by craft-focused effort. The next chapter names it as career capital.
explanation.competitive: The gains are stacking now. The next move is to define the currency.
